targets.name: PAN-OS Internal ICMP Host Discovery
targets.description: Detects one private source contacting at least 100 private destinations with ICMP within five minutes. This can indicate host discovery, but it is not proof of an attack.
targets.note:
## Investigation

Review the source system, number and range of destinations, time window, and whether the activity came from an approved monitoring system, vulnerability scanner, or network-management tool. Check for later port scans or service connections from the same source.

## Response

Confirm the source owner and whether the activity was scheduled or authorised. If it is unexplained, preserve the relevant logs and escalate to the SOC and system owner. Do not automatically block, isolate, reset passwords, or disable accounts based on this alert alone.
targets.query: event.dataset:"panw.panos" and panw.panos.type:"TRAFFIC" and event.action:"flow_started" and network.transport:"icmp" and source.ip:(10.0.0.0/8 or 172.16.0.0/12 or 192.168.0.0/16) and destination.ip:(10.0.0.0/8 or 172.16.0.0/12 or 192.168.0.0/16)

targets.name: Internal SSH Authentication Failure Burst
targets.description: Detects five failed SSH login attempts from the same source to the same host and username within ten minutes. This may indicate password guessing, but it does not prove that a login succeeded.
targets.note:
## Investigation

Review the source system, target host, username, authentication method, and exact time of the failures. Check whether the source is an approved administrator workstation, jump host, scanner, or penetration-test system. Look for successful logins immediately before and after the failures, and confirm the activity with the system owner.

## Response

If the activity is unexplained or unauthorised, preserve the relevant logs and escalate to the SOC and system owner for credential and host review. Do not automatically block, isolate, reset passwords, or disable accounts based on this alert alone.
targets.query: event.dataset:"system.auth" and event.action:"ssh_login" and event.outcome:"failure" and source.ip:* and user.name:*

targets.name: PAN-OS Repeated Sensitive-Service Access
targets.description: Detects one internal source contacting at least 10 distinct internal destinations on sensitive service ports 22, 23, 135, 139, 445, 3389, 5985, or 5986 within the rule window. This may indicate service discovery or remote-service probing, but it does not prove a successful login or compromise.
targets.note:
## Investigation

Review the source system, destination systems, ports, time window, connection results, and related alerts. Confirm whether the source is an approved vulnerability scanner, monitoring system, administrator workstation, or management tool. Check authentication logs and the destination owners to determine whether any access succeeded.

## Response

Confirm whether the activity was authorised. If it is unexplained or unauthorised, preserve the relevant logs and escalate to the SOC and system owners. Do not automatically block, isolate, reset passwords, or disable accounts based on this alert alone.
targets.query: event.dataset:"panw.panos" and panw.panos.type:"TRAFFIC" and panw.panos.action:allow and event.action:flow_started and destination.port:(22 or 23 or 135 or 139 or 445 or 3389 or 5985 or 5986) and source.ip:(10.0.0.0/8 or 172.16.0.0/12 or 192.168.0.0/16)
